0.long_answer: Sarcoglycanopathies, which are forms of limb‐girdle muscular dystrophy caused by mutations in one of the sarcoglycan genes (such as LGMD2C, LGMD2D, LGMD2E, and LGMD2F), may show decreased dystrophin levels on immunohistochemical testing. Even though the dystrophin gene itself is not mutated in these cases, disruption of the sarcoglycan complex can lead to secondary reductions in dystrophin expression. This immunohistochemical finding can therefore be observed as a helpful diagnostic clue in sarcoglycan-deficient forms of LGMD.
